title: Stage 4: The hotfix backport
summary: 16:00. Production (release/3.1) charges VAT twice on discounted items. The fix is on main; copy exactly that commit to the release branch.

steps.title: Briefing
body: Support reports double VAT in production. Production runs `release/3.1`. Marco already fixed it on `main` (commit `f1x` *fix: apply VAT once [backport]*), but `main` also contains features not ready to ship.
You need **only** `f1x` on `release/3.1`, recorded so anyone can trace it back:

steps.prompt: After `git cherry-pick -x f1x` on `release/3.1`, what does `git log --format=%B -1` print? (The full message of the new commit. The full hash of f1x is `f1x0000`.)
steps.explain: `-x` appends a blank line and the trailer naming the original commit, so the backport is traceable from the release branch.

steps.prompt: Why cherry-pick instead of merging `main` into `release/3.1`?
options: Merging would bring G and H, unreleased features, into production; cherry-pick copies only the fix
Merging is not allowed into release branches
steps.explain: Release branches take selected fixes only. The same fix then exists twice (f1x on main, f1x' on release), which merges cleanly later if ever needed.
Only fixes for bugs in the released version, flagged by whoever fixed them. Features and refactors wait for the next release.

steps.prompt: The release was `v3.1.0`. You add one backported fix and tag. What is the new tag? (Semantic versioning.)
steps.explain: A backwards-compatible bug fix bumps PATCH only.

steps.title: Find fixes that still need backporting
prompt: A release-manager script lists the commands to run. Write `ToBackport(mainCommits, releaseMessages)`:
- `releaseMessages`: full messages of commits already on the release branch.
- A main commit **needs** a backport if its subject starts with `fix` and contains `[backport]`, and no release message contains `(cherry picked from commit <its hash>)`.
Return `git cherry-pick -x <hash>` for each, oldest first.
starter: static List<string> ToBackport(List<(string Hash, string Subject)> mainCommits, List<string> releaseMessages)
solution: static List<string> ToBackport(List<(string Hash, string Subject)> mainCommits, List<string> releaseMessages)
hints: First collect the hashes already picked: find `(cherry picked from commit ` in each release message and read up to `)`.
Then filter `mainCommits` and format the command.
template: var dojoMain = new List<(string Hash, string Subject)> {
("ccc3", "fix: crash on empty basket [backport]"), ("ddd4", "fix: typo in admin page") };
var dojoRel = new List<string> { "fix: apply VAT once [backport]\n\n(cherry picked from commit bbb2)", "Release 3.1.0" };
Dojo.Eq("one still to pick", new List<string> { "git cherry-pick -x ccc3" }, ToBackport(dojoMain, dojoRel));
Dojo.Eq("nothing picked yet", new List<string> { "git cherry-pick -x bbb2", "git cherry-pick -x ccc3" }, ToBackport(dojoMain, new()));
